question.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R$ defined by

$$
f(x)={x}^{T}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot x,
$$

where the dot denotes matrix multiplication. What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x?$
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a scalar-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the row vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times n}.
$$

In our case, writing out the function $f(x)$ where $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} & 4{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times 2}.\end{aligned}
$$
